req.title: Update pre-populates form
req.statement: The system shall pre-fill the update form with the existing post's title and body.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-033 requires that GET /<id>/update pre-fills the update form with the existing post's title and body. Tests must verify: (1) positive — authenticated author sees their post's title and body in the response HTML; (2) negative — unauthenticated user is redirected (cannot see the form); (3) boundary — a post with minimal single-character title and body still pre-populates correctly; (4) negative — non-author authenticated user gets 403; (5) boundary — post with maximum-length title/body pre-populates fully. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (200 vs 302 vs 403 vs 404), exact byte strings from the known test data, and both sides of auth/author checks.

tests.name: test_update_prepopulates_form_authenticated_author
preconditions: User Rahul (id=1) is the author of post id=2 (title='Pillow delta willow', body='Zenith alpha vertex flux flux matrix harbor matrix.')
User is logged in as Rahul
expected: Response body contains 'Pillow delta willow' (the post title)
Response body contains 'Zenith alpha vertex flux flux matrix harbor matrix.' (the post body)
trace: R-FLASKR-033: system shall pre-fill update form with existing post title and body
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_update_prepopulates_form_authenticated_author():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Pillow delta willow' in r.data
    assert b'Zenith alpha vertex flux flux matrix harbor matrix.' in r.data

test_update_prepopulates_form_authenticated_author()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_update_prepopulates_after_state_transition_create():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/create', data={'title': 'Orbit beacon test', 'body': 'Summit flux delta.'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import get_db
        row = get_db().execute(
            "SELECT id FROM post WHERE title = 'Orbit beacon test' AND author_id = 1"
        ).fetchone()
        new_id = row['id']
    r = client.get(f'/{new_id}/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Orbit beacon test' in r.data
    assert b'Summit flux delta.' in r.data
